office.title: Indiana School Board Member
office.summary: A school board is the elected or appointed governing body of a public school corporation, the legal unit that runs a local school district [1, 2]. The board hires and evaluates the superintendent, adopts policies, and approves the annual budget, while the superintendent and staff run schools day to day [3]. Most boards have five or seven members serving staggered four-year terms [3]. Starting in 2026, candidates may list a political party, run as independents, or list no affiliation on the ballot, and there is no primary for these seats [2, 4].

facts.label: Term
facts.value: 4 years, with elections staggered so part of the board is chosen every two years [3]

facts.label: Elected
facts.value: At the November general election (November 3, 2026, or November 2028 for some seats); depending on the local organization plan, members represent the whole school corporation (at large) or a district within it, and some boards are wholly or partly appointed [2]

facts.label: Ballot label
facts.value: Each candidate chooses a party label, 'Independent', or no affiliation, shown next to the name; no primary and no straight-ticket voting for these races [2, 4]

facts.label: Pay
facts.value: Set by board resolution: an annual amount of no more than 10% of the lowest starting teacher salary in the school corporation, plus a capped per diem [5]

duties: Hires, evaluates and can dismiss the superintendent, and approves the hiring and firing of principals, teachers and other staff recommended by the superintendent [1, 7, 3].
Adopts the annual budget, appropriates funds and oversees school finances [1, 3].

Decides whether to ask voters to approve an operating referendum (an extra property tax levy); the board adopts the resolution and the Department of Local Government Finance reviews the ballot language for compliance with state law [8].
Approves contracts, buys and sells property, and decides on construction, repair and demolition of school buildings [1].

Bargains with the teachers' union over salary, wages and wage-related benefits such as health insurance and retirement; state law excludes teacher evaluation procedures from those bargaining subjects [9].
Writes and updates policies and rules for schools, often in a policy handbook, including the student handbook [1, 3].
Buys curricular materials, provides them to students without charge, and runs programs such as student transportation and school lunch [1].

Must adopt a process for parents and residents to ask that library material be removed as obscene or harmful to minors, review requests at public meetings and keep a public catalog of library materials [10].
Hears written appeals of student expulsions, unless the board has voted not to hear them [11].
Must take official action openly; Indiana's Open Door Law says public agencies' official action is to be conducted openly so the people may be fully informed [12, 13].

A school board member must have lived in the school corporation (and, for a district seat, the district) for at least one year before the election, and a teacher or other employee of the school corporation may not serve on its board [2].

What the board does not control: the State Board of Education adopts statewide academic standards [14], the General Assembly sets the state school funding formula in the state budget [15], and voucher (Choice Scholarship) eligibility is set by state law [16].
recent_changes: 2025: Senate Enrolled Act 287 allowed school board candidates to declare a party affiliation; the Indiana School Boards Association opposed the change, and a supporter quoted by WNDU, a Noblesville school board member, said it adds transparency [17].

2026: Candidates choose a party, 'Independent' or no affiliation on their nominating petition, and that choice appears on the ballot; a candidate claiming the Democratic or Republican party must have voted in that party's primary in the two most recent primaries they voted in, or have certification from the county party chair, or can be challenged and removed from the ballot [2].

July 2026: Chalkbeat reported, citing Indiana School Boards Association data, that 524 of 1,044 candidates chose a party, about 72% of them Republicans [18]; the Indiana Election Division's 2026 guidance and the wording of the law differ on the primary-voting test, a question county election boards decide [19].

February 2026: Senate Enrolled Act 25 set the order of school board candidates on the ballot, grouped by party, with candidates who list no affiliation placed after the party and independent candidates [20].

2025: Senate Enrolled Act 1, a property tax law, limits how much operating revenue districts can raise through taxes and restricts school referendums to statewide general elections in even-numbered years [21, 22].
2025: The same law requires districts to share operating revenue with brick-and-mortar charter schools that enroll their students, statewide starting in 2028 [21, 22].
2025: The state budget opened Choice Scholarship vouchers to all Indiana families starting in June 2026 [16].
2026: The Indianapolis Public Education Corporation, rather than the Indianapolis Public Schools board, now certifies Indianapolis Public Schools referendum questions for the ballot [20].

2023: Senate Enrolled Act 391 changed the so-called $1 law so the Indiana Department of Education can order districts that lost at least 10% of enrollment over five years to close schools under 60% capacity and offer them to charter schools [23].
2023: House Enrolled Act 1447 required school districts to set up procedures for complaints that library material is obscene or harmful to minors [10].

race_context: The district: South Adams Schools has its office at 1075 Starfire Way in Berne, Adams County, and runs an elementary, a middle and a high school [24]. South Adams High School was formed by consolidating the Berne, Geneva, Hartford Township and Jefferson Township high schools, and it had 347 students in 2024–25, according to Wikipedia [25]. This guide did not find a current districtwide enrollment figure.

Superintendent: Superintendent Michelle Clouser Penrod announced in July 2025 that she would retire after the 2025–26 school year, and Meyer was selected to replace her [26]. The district's notice for the Feb. 10, 2026 contract hearing summarized an agreement employing Joseph Meyer as superintendent from July 1, 2026, with a $118,000 base salary [27, 28]. The district site lists Joe Meyer as superintendent [24].

The board: there are seven members, and each seat has a defined area [29]. District I is west of County Road 000 and south of State Highway 218, not counting Berne and Geneva [29]. District II is east of County Road 000 and south of SR 218, also not counting Berne and Geneva [29]. District III is the City of Berne, District IV is the Town of Geneva, District V is north of SR 218 (not counting Berne), and District VI is at large [29]. The members are President Arlene Amstutz (II, term ends 2028), Vice President Adam Lehman (III, 2026), Secretary Landon Patterson (I, 2026), Rhonda Briggs (IV, 2028), Brian Caffee (V, 2028), Kyle Litwiller (VI, 2028) and Mitch Sprunger (III, 2026) [29]. At its first meeting of 2026, the board passed a motion to keep things the same for 2026 [30].

District 1 (one seat): this is a rematch [31]. In 2022 Landon Patterson defeated Benjamin M. Rediger 1,181 votes to 1,009 [31]. Patterson's term ends in 2026 [29]. On the 2026 state list, Rediger is labeled Republican and Patterson Independent [6].

District 3 (likely two seats): District III has two board members, Adam Lehman and Mitch Sprunger, and both terms end in 2026 [29]. In 2022 the District 3 race was 'Vote For 2,' and Lehman (1,791 votes) and Mitchel W. Sprunger (1,338) were the only candidates [31]. The state list shows District 3 as 'vote for 1,' with Adam S Lehman (Republican) and Mitch Sprunger (Nonpartisan) [6]. If both seats are on the ballot, as in 2022, both incumbents would be elected. This guide did not find a 2026 sample ballot to confirm. Both District 3 candidates are sitting members [29].
How candidates qualified: school board candidates filed petitions with the county clerk by noon on June 18, 2026 [32].

Budget and property taxes (2025–2026): the board approved its 2026 budget in October 2025 [33]. For 2027, the district's budget notice lists a total of $19,635,361: $11,820,875 for Education, $4,257,211 for Operations, $2,357,275 for Debt Service and $1,200,000 for the Rainy Day fund [34]. It also lists a property tax cap credit estimate of $539,000 and a maximum operating levy estimate of $3,739,580 [34]. The hearing was set for Aug. 18, 2026 and adoption for Oct. 13, 2026 [34]. The board held its 2027 budget workshop in July 2026 [35]. This guide did not find district statements on how SEA 1 affects South Adams.

Facilities and bonds (2025–2026): in October 2025 the board approved phase 2 of its facility improvement project [33]. In early 2026 the board discussed a sanitary project, auditorium lighting and upgrades, and authorizing and refinancing bonds [36, 28, 37]. The March 10, 2026 agenda included a review of bids for phase 2 of the sanitary project [37]. On April 14, 2026 it held a hearing on a '2026 Unified Project' covering renovations and improvements across the district, site work, and buying equipment, buses and technology [38, 39]. That meeting's agenda included a project resolution and a declaration of intent to reimburse expenditures [38, 39]. The board approved bids for summer projects in June 2026 and got construction updates in July [40, 41]. In August 2026 the district gave notice of a plan to issue about $7,780,000 in bonds to refinance its Series 2016 building corporation bonds [42, 43].

Teachers (2025–2026): the board held a public hearing on teacher pay and bargaining on Sept. 9, 2025, and a hearing on a tentative teacher contract on Nov. 4, 2025 [44, 45]. The district has posted a tentative 2026–27 master contract [24].

Policies and scheduling (2026): the March and April 2026 agendas included retiring all of the district's NEOLA policies and approving the Indiana School Boards Association's required policies [37, 39]. A February 2026 Berne Witness report said the board was divided over synchronous e-learning while discussing the 2026–27 calendar [46, 28]. In June 2026 administrators told the board about an attendance policy updated to match state standards [47]. In April 2026 a resident used the guest comment time to object to a Turning Point USA club [48].

School safety (2026): the board discussed a safety ordinance in January 2026 [36]. In May 2026 the school resource officer brought a traffic-enforcement ordinance for South Adams Schools to the Berne Board of Public Works and Safety [49]. In September 2026 the director of operations reported to the board on a mock disaster drill [50].
Forums: this guide found no candidate forums, questionnaires or news profiles of the 2026 South Adams candidates.

candidates.summary: Challenger for the District 1 seat, listed as Republican [6]. He lost the 2022 race for this seat to Landon Patterson [31].
background: Ran for the District 1 seat in 2022 (as Benjamin M Rediger) and received 1,009 votes (46%) to Patterson's 1,181 [31]. Ran for the at-large seat in 2024 and received 1,317 votes (41%), losing to Kyle Litwiller [51].
path_to_ballot: Listed as Republican on the state candidate list [6]. School board candidates qualified by petition filed with the county clerk by June 18, 2026 [32].

background: Board secretary [29]. His District I term ends in 2026 [29]. He won the seat in 2022, defeating Rediger 1,181 votes to 1,009 [31].
path_to_ballot: Listed as Independent on the state candidate list [6]. School board candidates qualified by petition filed with the county clerk by June 18, 2026 [32].
on_incumbent: Is a current board member and board secretary [29].
gaps: No campaign statements, website, questionnaire responses, endorsements or finance reports found.
His votes and stated views on board issues (such as the February 2026 e-learning debate) were not found. Board minutes and full Berne Witness articles were not available to this guide.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board vice president, running for reelection in District 3, listed as Republican [29, 6].
background: Board vice president [29]. His District III (City of Berne) term ends in 2026 [29]. He won in 2022 with 1,791 votes in a two-seat race with two candidates [31].
path_to_ballot: Listed as Republican on the state candidate list [6]. School board candidates qualified by petition filed with the county clerk by June 18, 2026 [32].
on_incumbent: Is a current board member and vice president [29].
gaps: No campaign statements, website, questionnaire responses, endorsements or finance reports found.
Not to be confused with South Adams assistant principal Jeff Lehman or State Rep. Matt Lehman, who appear in the same local coverage.

background: His District III (Berne) term ends in 2026 [29]. He won in 2022 (as Mitchel W Sprunger) with 1,338 votes in a two-seat race with two candidates [31].
